# gr-osmosdr

**One GNU Radio source block that speaks to nearly every SDR**

- **Version recorded:** 0.2.6
- **Categories:** `hardware`, `sdr`
- **Upstream:** <https://osmocom.org/projects/gr-osmosdr/wiki>
- **Needs first:** `gnuradio`

## What it does

Provides a single GNU Radio source and sink pair that talks to RTL-SDR, HackRF, Airspy, bladeRF, SDRplay, USRP, FunCube and several others, all behind one device-string interface. Change the string, not the flow graph.

## Why you would want it

Without it, every SDR needs its own source block and every flow graph is tied to the hardware it was drawn for. This is why a flow graph downloaded from someone with a HackRF runs on your RTL-SDR. It is also what gqrx and a good deal of other software use underneath.

## Before it will work

GNU Radio, and the driver library for whatever hardware you have -- this is a shim over those libraries, not a replacement for them.

## How it installs

- apt: `gr-osmosdr`

## Known problems

Which devices are actually supported depends on which driver libraries were present when the package was built, and an unsupported device fails to open with a message about the device string rather than about the missing driver. Development upstream has been slow, and SoapySDR is the newer answer to the same problem -- both are carried here because software in the wild uses both.

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
